title: Il Congiuntivo Presente: Formazione
subtitle: The mood of opinion, doubt and wish — how to build it.
objectives: Conjugate regular verbs in the congiuntivo presente
Recognize that the tu/lui/lei forms are identical, requiring the subject pronoun for clarity
Recognize common irregular subjunctive stems: essere, avere, andare, fare

content.intro: The subjunctive isn't a tense but a mood — it signals that what follows is an opinion, a wish, a doubt, or something not presented as objective fact, rather than a straightforward statement.
content.explanation: Formed from the io form of the present indicative (drop the -o, add the subjunctive endings). Almost every verb that's irregular in the present indicative keeps that same irregular stem in the subjunctive. One quirk worth knowing early: io, tu, and lui/lei all share the identical ending, so the subject pronoun is often needed to avoid ambiguity, breaking Italian's usual pro-drop habit.

rules.heading: b) Common irregular stems
rules.body: essere → sia, sia, sia, siamo, siate, siano; avere → abbia...; andare → vada...; fare → faccia...; potere → possa...; dovere → debba...; volere → voglia...; venire → venga...

rules.heading: c) When it's triggered
rules.body: Almost always inside a subordinate clause introduced by che, after a main clause expressing opinion, doubt, emotion, or will — covered in detail in the next lesson.

examples.it: Credo che sia una buona idea.
examples.en: I believe it's a good idea.

examples.it: È importante che voi arriviate in orario.
examples.en: It's important that you arrive on time.

examples.it: Non credo che loro vengano stasera.
examples.en: I don't think they're coming tonight.

commonMistakes.why: Penso che triggers the subjunctive, not the indicative ha.

commonMistakes.wrong: Spero che io sia felice. (ambiguous without context)
commonMistakes.right: Spero di essere felice. (same subject, use di + infinitive instead)
commonMistakes.why: When the subject of both verbs is the same, Italian prefers di + infinitive over che + subjunctive.
Volere che triggers the subjunctive: vada, not the indicative vai.

items.explanation: Irregular subjunctive stem of avere: abbia.
Irregular subjunctive stem of venire: venga.
Penso che always triggers the subjunctive.

summary: Io, tu and lui/lei share an identical form — keep the subject pronoun for clarity.
Most present-indicative irregular verbs keep the same irregular stem in the subjunctive.
